blocks.text: Dear Mr. Palmer:

This letter sets out the terms on which the firm will provide prosecution support for the patent portfolio of {{fact:f:E-2021-001.client}}, and it records the scope of that work, the people who will carry it, and the commercial terms that govern it. It follows our conversations this summer and the schedule of pending matters your office sent afterward. When you have signed and returned the enclosed copy, this letter becomes the agreement between us and supersedes anything discussed before it.
The Prosecution Support We Will Provide

Under this engagement we carry the active prosecution of the Keith-Duarte portfolio: drafting and filing the applications your office directs, preparing and filing responses to office actions as they issue, and keeping each family current so that no filing or response goes past its date. We take the pending matters in the order the docket sets, review each file history against the office record before we act on it, and return to you a short written update against the relevant matter whenever a family moves.

Some work sits outside this letter and is available under a separate engagement if you request it. Under this engagement we are not preparing freedom-to-operate or validity opinions, conducting portfolio-wide clearance, or litigating any matter; where the prosecution reaches a question that calls for one of those, we will tell you and stop rather than begin work you have not authorized. Nothing we file or advise under this letter is an opinion that any patent is valid, infringed, or clear to practice, and it should not be read or relied upon as one.
How We Will Carry the Work

The docket is the center of this work, and everything else is arranged around it. We calendar every deadline in the portfolio, confirm each date against the office record, and route nothing out and let no date pass without its clearing docketing first; a date, once confirmed, is not quietly moved. You will hear from us on a regular schedule and again whenever a response comes due, and each update will be tied to the matter it concerns, so that your file runs in order rather than as a single running narrative.
Who Will Do the Work

Heather Munoz, a partner in the prosecution group, leads the engagement and is responsible for what we file and for what we send you. Kelly Snyder, an associate, prepares the office-action responses and keeps the portfolio dockets reconciled against the office record, and Joseph Walker, an associate, works the specifications and file histories on the technical side of each matter. I read what leaves this office before it reaches you, as I do with all client work, and I am the person to call if at any point you are not satisfied with the work or with the people doing it.
Fees and Payment

Our fee for this engagement is {{fact:f:E-2021-001.fee}}, and the basis on which it is set is stated on the signature page you will execute with this letter. Work commences on {{fact:f:E-2021-001.start}}, subject to your signature and to our receiving the portfolio schedule, access to the prosecution files, and confirmation of who at {{fact:f:E-2021-001.client}} holds authority to approve a filing; we will not begin billing before that date.

We invoice monthly for the work of the preceding month, and each invoice is payable within thirty days of its date. If an invoice remains unpaid beyond its terms we may suspend work on the matter after written notice to you, and because the portfolio runs against live dates we will identify any deadline then at risk before we stop, so that a billing dispute never becomes a lost date.
Term and Termination

This agreement takes effect on the date you sign below and continues until the prosecution support described here is complete and our final invoice is paid. Either of us may end it earlier on written notice to the other. If the engagement ends before the work is finished, you will owe us for the work performed and the expenses incurred to that point, and we will hand over the file in the state it then stands together with a written note of what remains open and any date we know to be approaching.
Confidentiality

We will hold what you give us in confidence and use it only for this engagement, and access within the firm is limited to the people named above and to those whose work on the portfolio requires it. We will not disclose your information outside the firm without your consent, except where a court or another authority with jurisdiction compels it, and in that event we will tell you first if we are free to do so. Our written analysis is prepared as privileged work product for you, and these obligations continue after the engagement ends.
Limitation of Liability

Our liability to you arising out of this engagement, whether framed in contract or in negligence, will not exceed the total fees you pay us under it, except in the case of our fraud or willful misconduct. Neither of us will be liable to the other for indirect or consequential loss, including lost profits or lost opportunity, whether or not the possibility was known in advance. Our work rests on the accuracy and completeness of the records you and the patent offices provide; where those records are wrong or incomplete, the consequences of the error are not ours to carry, though we will tell you as soon as we have reason to doubt what we have been given.
Governing Law

This agreement is governed by the law of the state in which our office sits, without regard to its conflict-of-laws rules. Before either of us begins a proceeding, we will try to resolve the dispute through discussion between people with authority to settle it. This letter and its signature page are the whole of the agreement on their subject, and either may be changed only in a writing signed by both of us.

If these terms match your understanding, please sign both copies of the signature page, keep one for your file, and return the other to my office. If any term does not, telephone me and we will settle it before you sign. The one thing I need from you to open the work is the signed letter; return it and we will docket the portfolio and take up the first matter due.
Sincerely,

To: Kelly Snyder and Joseph Walker
From: Heather Munoz, Partner
Re: Kickoff, prosecution support for the Keith-Duarte portfolio
The goal on this engagement is narrow. We keep every family in the Keith-Duarte portfolio current, and we let no filing or response pass its date. Everything below serves that.

The client is {{fact:f:E-2021-001.client}}. Their contact is Joseph Palmer, their General Manager, and client questions route through him. The engagement runs from {{fact:f:E-2021-001.start}}, and we are at the front of it now.

One thing to fix before anything else. The docket is the part of this the firm cannot forgive. A date, once confirmed, is not moved to suit a draft, and no matter leaves this office without clearing the desk.
How the Work Divides
Owners are set now, so nothing sits between us. Each of you knows the whole of your part; read this before the first response comes due.

items: Docket and dates. Kelly Snyder pulls every deadline in the portfolio and reconciles it against the office record. Nothing is assumed. Each date is confirmed against the file, not the calendar we inherited.
Office actions. Kelly Snyder drafts the responses as actions issue, in the order the docket sets. I review each before it files. Nothing goes out on a Friday afternoon without a second read.

File histories and specifications. Joseph Walker reads into each family, checks the record behind every response, and flags anything in a specification the response has to account for. If the history does not support a position, we do not take it.
Client updates. Short notes against the matter, sent whenever a family moves. I write the ones the client reads. Keep your notes to me plain and dated, and I will shape what goes out.

blocks.text: Joseph Palmer hears from me, not from the desk, and not from a draft that has not been read. That is how a scope question stays a scope question and does not become a surprise.

Two things about how we write here. Do not overstate a response. A claim we cannot support in the record is a liability, not a win, and I would rather read a careful hedge than a confident one. Mark privileged work privileged without being asked.
The portfolio we inherited is in decent shape, but the inherited calendar is not the source of truth. The file is. Where the two disagree, the file wins and I want to know.
First Actions

Kelly Snyder: build the deadline calendar this week and send me anything due in the next thirty days. Joseph Walker: start on the two families closest to a response date and read their histories first. Both of you: bring me anything unclear before you act on it, not after.
The two families closest to a date come first. Everything else waits behind them until the calendar is built and I have seen it. Do not start a response on a family whose dates we have not confirmed.
Log every date you confirm against the source. If a date on the inherited calendar does not match the office record, stop and tell me. That mismatch is exactly the kind of thing we are here to catch.
We meet Friday to confirm the calendar. Bring the dates.
Dear Joseph,

I am opening this thread so our updates on the Keith-Duarte prosecution work stay in one place and your file runs in order against each matter. For the record, the working contacts are set: Joseph Palmer, General Manager, on your side, and on ours Kelly Snyder, who prepares the responses and holds the docket, and Joseph Walker, who works the file histories behind them.

We have made a start. The portfolio families are pulled and on the docket, and Kelly Snyder is reconciling each file history against the office record before the first responses go out. Two families will need responses first, and those are the ones we are reading now. Nothing in the portfolio is at its date in this window, and I will flag any deadline the moment one comes into view. You will hear from us on a set cadence, and each note will be tied to the family it concerns.

One request before the work goes further. Please confirm who at {{fact:f:E-2021-001.client}} can approve a filing if a response falls due, so we route it correctly the first time. A name and title is enough for now, and you can send it back to me on this thread.
Best

The portfolio is on schedule, and this session was about keeping it there through the winter filings rather than repairing anything that had slipped; we met to walk the Keith-Duarte families one at a time, confirm the dates coming due, and agree who carries each response, and we came out of it with the calendar unchanged and the next round of office-action work assigned.

Joseph Walker, Associate, Prosecution (minutes)
Joseph Palmer, General Manager, {{fact:f:E-2021-001.client}}

blocks.text: What We Covered

Heather Munoz opened by reminding us that we are about halfway through the engagement, and that the middle is where a portfolio quietly goes wrong if the docket is not watched, so we spent the first part of the session reconciling Kelly Snyder's calendar against the office record one family at a time and found no surprises, which is the outcome we want and rarely get to report without a caveat. Kelly Snyder walked the responses that have gone out since kickoff and the two that are drafted and waiting on a partner's read, and we agreed that nothing in the current window is at genuine risk, though we flagged one family where an examiner interview would probably save a round of prosecution and asked Heather Munoz to weigh whether it is worth the client's money.

On the technical side, I took the group through what I have found reading behind the responses, and the histories are clean enough that we are not fighting our own file, which matters more the deeper into examination we go; Kelly noted, fairly, that Joe tends to read further into a specification than a response strictly needs, and Heather Munoz's view was that on this portfolio the extra reading is cheap insurance and should continue. Joseph Palmer asked the practical questions a general manager asks, chiefly whether any of this threatens a date his board is watching, and we were able to tell him plainly that it does not, while being careful, as this firm is, not to promise an outcome the examiner still controls.

Before we closed we set the shape of the next stretch, which is mostly steady prosecution with two responses to file and a single decision for the client to make, and Heather Munoz asked that the action items reach Joseph Palmer the same day, so that nothing the client needs to see waits behind a memo that has to be written and circulated first. We also agreed, since we are at the point in a matter where small things start to accumulate, that Kelly Snyder would keep a running list of the open questions rather than let them collect in email, so that the next session starts from a single page instead of four separate threads none of us has read in full.
Action Items

rows: File the two drafted office-action responses once reviewed
Read into the newest family in the portfolio and flag what its first response must address
Decide whether to request an examiner interview on the flagged family
Keep the running list of open questions for the next session
Send these minutes and the open dates to Joseph Palmer

blocks.text: The one thing that has to happen before we meet again is Heather Munoz's call on the examiner interview, since both responses and the client's decision hang off it, so that is where we start next time.
Status Report: Keith-Duarte Prosecution Support
Prepared by Heather Munoz, Partner, for {{fact:f:E-2021-001.client}}. This report covers the current period and is written against the portfolio docket, matter by matter.
Where the Engagement Stands

The engagement is on schedule and on budget. We are roughly halfway through the work, every family in the portfolio is docketed and current, and no deadline has been missed or is at risk in the near window.

Nothing on the matter needs a decision from you this period. One decision is coming next period, and it is described below so you can see it before it arrives. The rest is routine prosecution, which is where a portfolio should sit at this stage.
Who Is on the Matter

The same three people who started the engagement are still on it. Kelly Snyder prepares the responses and holds the docket, and Joseph Walker works the file histories and specifications behind them. I lead the matter and read everything before it reaches you.

This is deliberate. The people who met you at the start are the people doing the work, and that does not change partway through a matter at this firm. If you ever want to talk to any of them directly, tell me and I will set it up.
What We Completed This Period

The work this period was steady prosecution, not firefighting. Each item below is filed or done and reflected on the docket. Kelly Snyder and Joseph Walker carried the bulk of it, and I read each response before it went out.

items: Kelly Snyder filed the office-action responses that were due and reconciled the full portfolio docket against the office record.
Joseph Walker read the file histories behind each response and confirmed the claim amendments are supported by the specifications.
We opened the one continuation the portfolio needed and docketed its new dates.
We corrected two dates on the calendar we inherited that did not match the office record. Neither was at risk, but both are now right.
Every family now has a confirmed date and an owner, so nothing sits unassigned.

blocks.text: The correction is worth a line. An inherited calendar is a starting point, not a source of truth, so we confirm every date against the file before we rely on it. Both mismatches were small and neither cost you anything. That is the point of doing the reconciliation early rather than discovering it late.
What Comes Next
The next period is more of the same, with two responses coming due and one decision we will bring to you. The plan is below.

items: Kelly Snyder will draft and file the two responses now on the calendar.
Joseph Walker will read into the newest family before its first response is due.
We will bring you a single decision on whether an examiner interview is worth pursuing on one family, with the cost and the likely benefit laid out so you can choose.

blocks.text: The interview question is the only one that needs you next period. An interview can save a round of prosecution on the flagged family, but it costs time and does not always land. We will send you the case for and against, and a number, before we do anything.
Risks

There is no material risk to report this period. The portfolio runs against live dates, so the standing risk is always a missed deadline, and our answer to it is the docket discipline described above.

If any family draws a response deadline shorter than usual, we will tell you at once rather than wait for the next report. The same holds for anything an examiner raises that changes the shape of a family. You will not learn of a problem from a status report for the first time.
Budget

The engagement fee is {{fact:f:E-2021-001.fee}}, and the work is tracking within it. At the halfway point we have used a little under half of that amount, which is where a steady prosecution matter should sit at this stage.

If anything above would take the work beyond the fee, we will tell you and quote it before we begin rather than bill you past the number you agreed to. The examiner interview is the one item that could do that, and we will price it for you as a separate line rather than fold it in.

We will send the next report at the usual interval, and the one item that may need you before then is the interview decision, which we will put in front of you as soon as it is ripe. Call me if anything here needs more than a report can give.

We are at the end of the engagement, and this session was a closeout rather than a working meeting: we walked the Keith-Duarte portfolio one last time to confirm that every family is where it should be, that nothing is left open without an owner, and that the record we hand back is clean enough for the next person who opens it, and we finished satisfied on all three counts.

blocks.text: What We Covered

Heather Munoz took us through the portfolio one family at a time, and the picture is the one we set out to reach: the office-action responses that were live at kickoff are filed and docketed, the families that needed a continuation have it, and there is no deadline in the near window that this engagement leaves unattended. Kelly Snyder confirmed that the docket is fully reconciled against the office record and that every date now on the calendar is recorded with a clear note of what it is and what it needs, so that nothing we were carrying is left to be reconstructed later from memory.

I walked the file histories one last time to be sure the record we are handing back reads cleanly, and it does; the responses track the examiners' rejections without overreaching, the claim amendments are supported by the specifications, and there is nothing in the wrapper a future reader would have to explain away, which is the standard this firm holds itself to on the way out of a matter as much as the way in. Joseph Palmer told us the portfolio is in the shape his board wanted at this stage and asked only that the closing summary be concrete about which applications remain in examination and which are through it, so that his team can brief the board without our having to be in the room.

We agreed that the closeout package will be a short written summary organized the way we ran the work, family by family, with the open dates listed plainly and nothing dressed up as more settled than it is, and Kelly Snyder and I will build it this week for Heather Munoz to read before it reaches the client. We also spent a few minutes on the handoff itself, because a portfolio is only as good as the record the next person inherits, and we made sure the docket carries not just the dates but a plain note beside each one so that whoever opens the file after us does not have to call to learn what a date means.
Action Items

rows: Assemble the family-by-family closeout summary with all open dates listed
Check every file history once more before the summary is finalized
Review the closeout summary before it goes to the client
Send the final summary and open-date list to Joseph Palmer

blocks.text: The one thing that has to happen before we close the file is Heather Munoz's read of the summary, so that is the last gate, and once it clears the engagement is complete and the record is the client's to keep.
